mappings.note: Definition of 'biogeochemical cycle' as cyclic movement between abiotic and biotic components - C4.3's interactions clause. Distinguished from N9/S102/S107 purely by the absence of any drawing demand, which is what LO-56 requires.

Why VISIBLE light specifically matters: it is the band that drives photosynthesis. The discriminator is which part of the spectrum (LO-3), not how much arrives (LO-2). C4.3 carries the biological use.

Defining feature of the exosphere. POOR FIT: pure atmospheric-structure recall with no mechanism, no radiation and no cycle. The frame simply has no outcome for the vertical structure of the atmosphere.

Anna Mani mapped solar INSOLATION - the quantity of solar radiation reaching India's surface, which is LO-2. The history-of-Indian-science half belongs to CG6, which is not in this chapter's legal set, so it goes uncited.
Define the biosphere. LO-55's fragment lists the biosphere by name and is the only code that does. A two-mark definition with no process, so nothing else in the frame applies.
Define the cryosphere. Same outcome as V59 and honestly so - LO-55 is a bare list of the five spheres, so every define-a-sphere item lands on it and nothing can split them.

'Name the type of waves' - the answer is electromagnetic waves, which is LO-3's own assertion. LO-2 is the more general 'nature of solar radiation', but LO-3 states the wave/frequency fact this item asks for exactly.

Value of the solar constant. Recall of the incoming beam's magnitude, LO-2. Unlike O8 and L121 there is nothing to compute, so C8.1 is withheld - that calculation demand is the discriminator inside this family.

Asks for the term 'albedo'. LO-5's surface-interaction clause is the only outcome that touches reflection by a surface. Shares its code with the rest of the albedo family, which the frame gives no means of splitting.

Why snow and ice stay cold: high albedo reflects most of the incoming radiation. Same LO-5 clause as V63, but the demand is the consequence rather than the term - a distinction the frame cannot express with a second code.

Cause of the urban heat island: concrete and asphalt absorb and later release solar radiation. LO-5's surface clause. Not LO-4 - a city's heat has nothing to do with the Earth's shape, latitude or tilt.
One difference in temperature trend between the two lowest layers. The structural fact has no outcome (C2.8); the stated cause of the stratospheric inversion is ultraviolet absorption, which is LO-3.

The ozone layer's function is absorbing the UV band specifically - band-selective absorption, LO-3. The layer's location in the stratosphere has no outcome, but the function asked for is squarely LO-3's.

Name a greenhouse gas and state its role. The role - trapping the infrared the surface re-radiates - is LO-5's interaction clause. The gas's identity has no outcome anywhere in the frame, which is why only one code is cited.

Earth with no atmosphere would be far too cold, because nothing would retain the heat the surface radiates away - LO-5's re-radiation clause read in reverse. C2.8 carries the habitability consequence.
Cause of the daytime valley breeze. LO-5 names the valley breeze explicitly. Two marks, mechanism only - no diagram, so LO-56 stays out, which is what separates it from S112.

How a mountain breeze differs from a valley breeze. LO-5 names BOTH in a single clause, so the outcome cannot discriminate between the two directions the question contrasts. Fused-row defect, recorded rather than worked around.

The Earth's rotation deflecting planetary winds. POOR FIT: winds are 'air movement' in LO-5, but the actual content - Coriolis deflection - is absent from every outcome in this frame, LO-4 included (it names tilt, not spin).
Define ocean gyres. POOR FIT: rotation acting on the hydrosphere, neither of which has an outcome. Cited at competency level with O32, O16, O40 and S101 for the same documented gap.

The Gulf Stream's climatic significance - warm equatorial water carried poleward, a differential-heating consequence (LO-5) travelling through the ocean (C2.8). Separated from V73 by being about heat, not about rotation.

What a biogeochemical cycle means in an ecosystem - matter moving between abiotic and biotic components, C4.3. Paired with O55; both are definitions, and neither triggers LO-56 because nothing is drawn.

Sea-level rise is explained as glacier melt adding water to the oceans - a cryosphere-to-hydrosphere transfer, and LO-55 is the only code naming those two spheres. Not LO-5: the warming is given, not derived from solar radiation.
Names photosynthesis as the process converting CO2 to glucose. A single biological step in the fast carbon cycle, C4.3. No cycle diagram and no human impact, so neither LO-56 nor C2.8 is engaged.

Burning fossil fuels returns long-stored geological carbon to the air. My fast/slow rule sends the geological reservoir and human perturbation to C2.8; C4.3 is withheld because no living organism is involved in the step being tested.

Anna Mani's solar radiation atlas - the mapped quantity is insolation, LO-2. Same code as O58 because the same scientific content is being recalled; the biography half again falls to CG6, which is outside this frame.
